title: 3D Double Pendulum Chaos Simulation and Phase Space Visualization
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a 3D double pendulum chaotic physics simulation and synchronously plot its phase-space trajectory.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
// Write your code here
</script>

[Double Pendulum Physics Model (Lagrangian Mechanics, Must Be Implemented Precisely)]
The system consists of two rigid rods and point masses:
- Rod 1: length L1=2.0m, endpoint mass m1=1.0kg, angle θ1 (measured from the vertically downward direction)
- Rod 2: length L2=1.5m, endpoint mass m2=1.0kg, angle θ2 (measured from the vertically downward direction)
- Gravitational acceleration g=9.81 m/s²

Exact formulas for angular acceleration (results derived from the Lagrange equations):
α1 = [-g(2m1+m2)sin(θ1) - m2·g·sin(θ1-2θ2) - 2sin(θ1-θ2)·m2·(ω2²L2 + ω1²L1cos(θ1-θ2))] / [L1·(2m1+m2-m2cos(2θ1-2θ2))]
α2 = [2sin(θ1-θ2)·(ω1²L1(m1+m2) + g(m1+m2)cos(θ1) + ω2²L2·m2·cos(θ1-θ2))] / [L2·(2m1+m2-m2cos(2θ1-2θ2))]

Numerical integration: use the 4th-order Runge-Kutta method (RK4) with a fixed time step of dt=0.005s. Execute multiple RK4 steps per rendered frame so that physics time remains synchronized with real time.

Initial conditions: θ1=120°(2π/3 rad), θ2=90°(π/2 rad), ω1=0, ω2=0

[3D Visualization]
(1) Left side (x<0 region): physical animation of the 3D double pendulum
  - Place the fixed pivot at (0, 5, 0), represented by a small sphere
  - Rod 1: a cylinder from the pivot to mass1 (yellow)
  - Rod 2: a cylinder from mass1 to mass2 (cyan)
  - mass1: a red sphere (radius 0.2)
  - mass2: a blue sphere (radius 0.2)
  - Motion trail of mass2: use THREE.Line to draw a trail containing the most recent 2000 position points (gradient color, from dark to bright)

(2) Right side (x>0 region): 2D Phase Space Diagram
  - Use a vertical PlaneGeometry as the canvas background (located at x=8)
  - The X-axis represents θ2 (range -π to π), and the Y-axis represents ω2 (range -10 to 10)
  - Use THREE.Points to draw phase-space trajectory points in real time (the most recent 5000 points)
  - Add axis labels and tick marks to the phase-space canvas

[Interactive Features]
(3) Drag to set initial angles: dragging mass1 or mass2 with the mouse sets the initial angles (pause the simulation while dragging, and restart from the new angles upon release)
(4) Speed slider: place a slider at the bottom of the page (id="speedSlider", range 0.1-5.0, default 1.0) to control the simulation speed multiplier
(5) Pause/play button (id="pauseBtn"): toggle the simulation between paused and playing states
(6) Reset button (id="resetBtn"): restore the initial angles and clear the trails
(7) Button to switch to the second set of initial conditions (id="perturbBtn"): slightly adjust θ1 by +0.001 rad (leaving everything else unchanged) to demonstrate chaotic sensitivity—an extremely small difference in initial conditions results in completely different trajectories

[HUD and State Exposure]
(8) The upper-left HUD displays the following information, updated in real time:
  - θ1 angle value (id="theta1", displayed to 3 decimal places)
  - θ2 angle value (id="theta2", displayed to 3 decimal places)
  - ω1 angular velocity (id="omega1")
  - ω2 angular velocity (id="omega2")
  - Total system energy E (id="energy") = T + V (kinetic energy + potential energy)
  - Simulation time (id="simTime", seconds)

(9) Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame with the following fields:
  - theta1, theta2: current angles (radians)
  - omega1, omega2: current angular velocities
  - mass1Pos: {x, y, z}, mass2Pos: {x, y, z}
  - totalEnergy: total system energy (kinetic energy + potential energy), which should be conserved under undamped conditions
  - simTime: simulation time (seconds)
  - isPaused: whether the simulation is paused
  - speedMultiplier: speed multiplier
  - trailLength: number of trail points

[Energy Conservation Verification]
The system is undamped, so the total energy E = T + V must be strictly conserved. Allowing for accumulated numerical integration error, the energy drift after 10 seconds of simulation must be < 1%.
Total kinetic energy T = 0.5·m1·(L1·ω1)² + 0.5·m2·[(L1·ω1)² + (L2·ω2)² + 2·L1·L2·ω1·ω2·cos(θ1-θ2)]
Total potential energy V = -(m1+m2)·g·L1·cos(θ1) - m2·g·L2·cos(θ2) (taking the pivot as the zero-potential-energy plane)

Output a single standalone HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
